answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 14 px wide from row 0 to row 29. Rows 2-5 are a light-blue header strip. The dark row 6 is the top of the screen bezel (the dark frame around the screen), not an eave shadow under a top surface. Everything below is vertical front detail: screen rows 7-14, slots at rows 17-21, a dark slot at rows 22-23 and a gold tray at rows 26-27. There is no ellipse and no roof or contents. A header strip plus a flat front face with no depth cue gives no top surface, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small blue kiosk with a lighter screen, a panel and a dark navy edge. The edge is a tinted dark blue of the body, not neutral black: 0% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral. Its blue body ramp has about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep), plus a screen and slot detail. The measured facts back this up. It has 11 visible tones per full tile, above prop-hedge (9) and below prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). Its near-flat coverage is 0%, so it has no large flat fills. It has fewer total colours (17 vs 38-40 for the richest references), which is expected for a locked palette on a small, simple object. It is a little less textured than the stall and well, but it does not look like a sticker. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the hedge and the lamp.
